newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: YACHTING - REPAIRED AMERICAS CUP BACK WITH NZ HOLDERS.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING - REPAIRED AMERICAS CUP BACK WITH NZ HOLDERS.

text.p: The America's Cup, yachting's most prestigious trophy, returned to its holders the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron on Monday, restored by its British makers after a sledge hammer attack in March.

Richard Jarvis, the managing director of Crown jewellers Garrard, who personally escorted the 150-year-old trophy back to Auckland after 12 weeks of intensive restoration in London, called the repairs "a labour of love".
"We have a great affection for this trophy," he told an audience gathered amid tight security to watch the handover.
Garrard had carried out the silver repairs to the trophy, known as the Auld Mug, after it was thoroughly beaten and bent.
The man charged with the sledge hammer attack, Benjamin Peri Nathan, is due to stand trial in Auckland District Court in September.
Nathan, a 28-year-old student and Maori activist, has pleaded not guilty to damaging the trophy and entering the yacht club building with intent to commit a crime.

Although the squadron now plans tighter security for the cup in its trophy room, and is awaiting delivery of a glass case being manufactured in Germany, the relic will spend the next few weeks touring New Zealand to promote the America's Cup defence planned for 1999 and 2000.
The cup will visit 17 towns and cities over two months and will be transported by armoured car.
"The cup's never had security like this," Team New Zealand spokesman Alan Sefton told reporters.
The team, headed by Sir Peter Blake, will defend its 1995 victory when it saw off Dennis Conner's Young America 5-0 in San Diego.
